title: CrossLinear: Plug-and-Play Cross-Correlation Embedding for Time Series Forecasting with Exogenous Variables

problem.claim: Time series forecasting with exogenous variables requires modeling dependencies between variables.

gap.claim: Traditional models often struggle to differentiate between endogenous and exogenous variables, causing inefficiency and overfitting.

contributions.claim: CrossLinear introduces a plug-and-play cross-correlation embedding module for Linear-based forecasting.
The module captures time-invariant and direct variable dependencies with minimal computational cost, while disregarding time-varying or indirect dependencies.
CrossLinear combines patch-wise processing with a global linear head to capture short-term and long-term temporal dependencies.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CrossLinear and its cross-correlation embedding module as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 12 real-world datasets reportedly show superior performance in short-term and long-term forecasting tasks.
The ablation study reportedly supports the effectiveness of the cross-correlation embedding module.
The authors report that the module generalizes as a plug-in for forecasting tasks across different domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Forecasting with exogenous variables presents challenges in modeling inter-variable dependencies.
Traditional models may fail to distinguish endogenous and exogenous variables, leading to inefficiency and overfitting.
CrossLinear addresses the challenge with a lightweight plug-and-play cross-correlation embedding module.
Patch-wise processing and a global linear head target short-term and long-term temporal dependencies.
The authors report results from 12 real-world datasets, an ablation study, and cross-domain plug-in generalizability.

source_observation.claim: The method models time-invariant and direct dependencies while excluding time-varying or indirect dependencies.

interpretation.claim: Restricting dependency modeling may reduce overfitting when broader dependency structures are difficult to estimate reliably.

application.claim: In forecasting systems, consider lightweight dependency modules that impose explicit selectivity over which variable relationships are modeled.

exception.claim: This approach may omit useful time-varying or indirect dependencies.

source_observation.claim: The module is designed as a plug-in for existing neural networks and various forecasting tasks.

interpretation.claim: Modular forecasting components can facilitate reuse across architectures and domains.

application.claim: When extending forecasting systems, evaluate reusable modules that can be integrated without replacing the surrounding architecture.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish generalizability beyond the reported forecasting tasks and domains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 12 datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not provide ablation configurations or computational-cost measurements.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility details.
